harmonicFunction: Am creates the mournful, introspective tonal center
Chromatic descent A -> G -> F# -> F provides an inevitable weeping gravity
The major IV chord (D) introduces a subtle Dorian color before resolving to the dominant E
Modulation to A major in the bridge provides emotional catharsis and light

techniques.name: Descending Line Cliché & Bassline Movement
techniques.description: Holding an Am chord grip while stepping the bass note down chromatically (A -> G -> F# -> F) using pinky and thumb fret-hand positioning.

notes: Anchor your index and middle fingers on strings 2 and 4 of the Am shape
Use open A for bar 1, ring/pinky for G on string 6, and thumb or index for F# and F
Ensure top strings continue ringing cleanly to sustain the chordal harmony
Maintain a steady folk-rock eighth-note fingerpicking or arpeggiated strum
sequence: Strike open A string root, followed by treble pluck across strings 3, 2, 1
Fret 3rd fret low E string (G) for Am/G while keeping upper chord voicing
Shift to 2nd fret low E string (F#) for Am/F#
Land on 1st fret low E string (F) for Fmaj7 before turning around through G, D, and E
tips: Keep fret-hand fingers arched so open strings do not get muted
Emphasize the lowest note on beat 1 of each measure to highlight the descending bass motion
Practice the transition from Am/F# to Fmaj7 slowly to build fret-hand dexterity

techniques.name: Soulful Blues Bending & Vocal Vibrato
techniques.description: Eric Clapton's legendary guest solo performance, featuring wide whole-step bends on the G string, finger vibrato, and Leslie rotating speaker tone simulation.

notes: Support string bends with 2nd and 1st fingers behind the 3rd finger for maximum pitch stability
Apply wide, singing finger vibrato at the peak of sustained bends
Incorporate slight rake strokes into target notes for aggressive attack
Balance major and minor pentatonic notes across the 5th and 7th fret positions
sequence: Bend 7th fret G string up a full step to E with crying vibrato
Release cleanly down to D and pull off to C (5th fret)
Resolve down to root note A on 7th fret D string
Execute double-stop bends on frets 5 and 7 of the high B and E strings
tips: Match pitch precisely against target frets before bending
Let the vibrato oscillate from the wrist rather than fingers alone
Use a warm overdrive with slight Leslie modulation or chorus to match the White Album track

sections.name: Intro Line Cliché & Piano Hook
sections.description: The haunting opening progression establishing the descending bass movement underneath an evocative A minor harmony.
notes: Play open A string root, then step down to G, F#, and F on the low E string
Keep the upper notes of the Am triad ringing continuously
Sets the melancholic, reflective mood of George Harrison's masterpiece

sections.name: Verse Rhythm & Strumming Mechanics
sections.description: Harrison's vocal entry supported by acoustic strumming and subtle electric guitar fills accenting the harmony.
sections.progression: Am - Am/G - Am/F# - Fmaj7 - Am - G - D - E
notes: Light down-up acoustic strumming with emphasis on downbeats
The D major chord provides a fleeting Dorian brightness before the dominant E pulls back to minor
Dynamic control is crucial—keep the acoustic rhythm steady under the vocal

sections.name: Bridge Parallel Major Shift
sections.description: The mood lifts radiantly as the song modulates to A Major, cycling through diatonic chords in a sweeping emotional release.
sections.progression: A - C#m - F#m - C#m - Bm - E - Bm - E
notes: Shift from A minor to bright open A Major chord
Barre chords C#m (4th fret) and F#m (2nd fret) require clean finger posture
The turnaround through Bm and E creates a strong cadence returning to the verse

sections.name: Main Verse & Crying Guitar Fills
sections.description: Eric Clapton's electric guitar begins entering between vocal phrases with weeping bends and expressive vibrato.
sections.progression: Am - Am/G - Am/F# - Fmaj7 - Am - G - D - E
notes: Tasteful fills nestled in vocal pauses
G string whole-step bend at the 7th fret mimicking a human sob
Subtle pick-hand palm muting for articulate dynamic response

sections.name: Eric Clapton Signature Guitar Solo
sections.description: One of the most famous guest guitar solos in rock history—flawless blues phrasing, singing bends, and exquisite note selection.
sections.progression: Am - Am/G - Am/F# - Fmaj7 - Am - G - D - E
notes: Position 1 A minor pentatonic centered at the 5th-8th frets
Climbs dynamically into the octave box at the 12th-15th frets
Wide pitch vibrato created by pivoting the entire fret-hand wrist
Recorded with Clapton's 1957 Gibson Les Paul ('Lucy') run through a flanged Leslie speaker

sections.name: Outro Climax & Solo Jam
sections.description: Clapton unleashes an extended blues-rock masterclass as the track builds to a roaring climax and fades out.
sections.progression: Am - Am/G - Am/F# - Fmaj7 - Am - G - D - E (fade out)
notes: Rapid blues pentatonic runs in the 17th-20th fret upper register
Unison bends on strings 1 and 2 adding intensity
Seamless interplay between rhythm acoustic and screaming lead guitar

beginner.title: Mastering the Descending Line Cliché
steps: Learn standard open Am, G, D, and E chords cleanly
Practice shifting the bass note from open A to G, F#, and F
Play through the verse progression at 50 BPM with a metronome
Strum steadily on quarter notes without muting adjacent strings

intermediate.title: Bridge Modulation & Soulful Fills
steps: Master the transition from A minor to the A major bridge
Clean up C#m and F#m barre chord transitions
Practice Clapton's signature vocal fills in position 1 pentatonic
Focus on accurate whole-step pitch bends on the G string

advanced.title: The Full Clapton Solo & Outro Improvisation
steps: Execute Clapton's studio solo with authentic vocal vibrato
Incorporate double-stop bends and rapid blues runs at 66 BPM
Tackle the high-register 17th-20th fret outro lead lines
Dial in authentic Leslie rotating speaker modulation and tube breakup

commonMistakes: Letting the open B and high E strings get muted during the descending bassline shifts
Under-bending the 7th fret G string in Clapton's signature crying lick
Rushing the tempo—the song has a laid-back, heavy 66 BPM groove that requires patience
Over-saturating the distortion—Clapton's tone comes from volume, touch, and the Leslie speaker
practiceRoutine: 5 mins: Chromatic finger independence warm-up on lower strings
10 mins: Slow practice of the Am -> Am/G -> Am/F# -> Fmaj7 chord changes
10 mins: Pitch-accuracy bend training on the 7th fret G string and 8th fret B string
15 mins: Playing along with Clapton's primary solo phrases at half speed
10 mins: Running through the complete song structure with metronome at 66 BPM
focusAreas: Fret-hand thumb and pinky bassline positioning
Pitch accuracy on whole-step string bends
Dynamic sensitivity between rhythm acoustic and lead electric
metronomeWork: Practice verse descending progression at 50 BPM with click on beats 2 and 4
Increase gradually to recording tempo of 66 BPM
Practice sixteenth-note blues solo flourishes cleanly with no rushing
